rootCause: The complete transaction log/segment/fallback/recovery implementation was packaged but never assembled by its auto-configuration; only lightweight context projections were beans.
The canonical transaction LoggingAspect matched CPF-internal Controller packages but not customer Generated Controllers annotated with CpfOnlineTransaction.
The first repair retained the legacy broad Controller name pointcut, which made Spring CGLIB-proxy intentionally final transport and management Controllers.
repair: Activate the complete persisted observability owner through explicit auto-configuration beans only when the platform transaction manager and all three concrete persistence/projection ports exist.
Observe package-independent CpfOnlineTransaction boundaries and the official CpfDomainOperation.invoke boundary, not Controller naming conventions.
Generate proxyable typed Domain operation adapters so remote and same-JVM invocation cross the same canonical AOP boundary.
safety: No DB Provider means no persisted observability component scan.
No mock or no-op persistence port is created.
Existing durable file fallback and recovery components remain the failure owner.
